name: Decline Cable Flye
description: The decline cable flye isolates the lower and sternal portions of the pectoralis major using a cable machine set at a low pulley angle combined with a decline bench. By lying on a decline bench and pressing handles from a low cable angle, the arc of motion closely matches the lower fiber direction of the pectoralis major, creating targeted stretch and contraction.

execution.starting_position: Position a decline bench between two low cable pulleys. Lie on the bench with feet secured. Hold a cable handle in each hand, arms extended to sides at approximately chest level, with a slight bend in the elbows.
execution.setup_instructions: Set both pulleys to the lowest position. Attach single-grip handles. Position the decline bench so that the cables create a low-to-inward pull angle when you lie on it.
steps: Step 1: Lie on the decline bench with arms extended out to the sides, slight elbow bend, handles gripped with palms facing up.
Step 2: Drive both handles upward and inward in a wide arc, maintaining the same elbow angle.
Step 3: Bring handles together above your lower chest, squeezing the pectorals at peak contraction.
Step 4: Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position, feeling the stretch across the lower chest.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you bring the handles together. Inhale during the return phase.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows too much and converting to a pressing motion
Allowing the arms to drop below the bench level, overstressing the shoulder
Using too much weight, compromising the arc of motion
safety_considerations: Keep elbows slightly bent and fixed — do not straighten or flex them during the rep
Secure feet firmly on the decline bench to prevent sliding
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Open arms to full stretch at the bottom (cable level), close to full adduction at the top. Avoid hyperextension at shoulder.
coaching_cues: Pretend you are hugging a large tree
The elbows never change their angle — only the shoulder joint moves
